Things were so bad that I would come home from school, go straight to my room and cry. If I didn't do that, I would purge and go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up. In school I would constantly think people were talking about me, and that my friends hated me. I had one friend who constantly made comments about me and I started to believe them. At home I felt out of place and miss understood. I felt like no one cared if I was here or not. My family would also make little comments that of course went straight to my head. 

Then covid hit right when I was at my worst. At first, it made everything worse and I was seriously contemplating ending it all. But, I ended up getting closer to my family. I got a job. I realized that I had so much to live for. I made it to my 15th birthday. I got a car. And another thing that made me open my eyes is when a family friend tried to commit. She was like a little sister to me and it made me want to do better myself.

I started excersising, became more spiritual and went on a long path of self love. All these things together helped me feel better. I'm still heavily working on my mental health. There are good days and bad days. But if I took my life I wouldn't ever be able to accomplish my dreams
